facts.content: Patient has a 3-day history of watery diarrhea occurring approximately once every hour when awake.
facts.source_text: CC: 3-day hx watery diarrhea (~q1h when awake)

facts.content: Patient experiences mid to lower abdominal cramp preceding stool, intermittent and rated around 6/10.
Patient reports no blood in stools.
Patient experiences nausea and occasional vomiting which worsens with milk.
Patient feels febrile but temperature has not been taken.
Patient reports decreased urine frequency.
Patient is attempting oral hydration but fluids seem to go straight through.
facts.source_text: Attempting oral hydration; fluids “go straight through”

facts.content: Patient's brother had a similar illness for 5 days and is now improving.
facts.source_text: Brother had similar illness x5 d, now improving

facts.content: Patient reports no past medical history.
Patient takes paracetamol as needed.
Patient has no known allergies.
Patient's father has stage III colon cancer.
Patient lives with mother and sister and has an office job in government.
facts.source_text: SH: lives w/ mother & sister; office job (government)

facts.content: Patient smokes socially and occasionally drinks alcohol heavily 1–2 times per month.
Acute gastroenteritis with high stool frequency and risk of dehydration.
facts.source_text: 1. Acute gastroenteritis w/ high stool frequency, risk dehydration

facts.content: Possible mild dehydration due to subjective reports of decreased urine frequency and feeling hot.
facts.source_text: 2. Possible mild dehydration (subjective ↓ urine, feeling hot)

facts.content: Family history of colorectal cancer noted for information.
Use oral rehydration salts (Dioralyte) freely; aim for pale yellow urine.
facts.source_text: Oral rehydration salts (Dioralyte) ad lib; aim urine pale yellow

facts.content: Advise clear fluids transitioning to a soft diet like soup and mashed food as tolerated.
facts.source_text: Clear fluids → soft diet (soup, mash) as tolerated

facts.content: Continue paracetamol as needed for pain or fever.
Avoid dairy and alcohol until recovery.
Contact GP or ED for red flags such as persistent vomiting, inability to keep fluids down, bloody stool, worsening pain, fever over 38°C, or no improvement in less than 48 hours.
facts.source_text: Red flags → contact GP/ED: persistent vomiting, inability to keep fluids, bloody stool, worsening pain, fever >38 °C, no improvement <48 h

facts.content: Follow-up telephone call if symptoms not settling in 48 hours or if there are concerns.
facts.source_text: Follow-up tel call if symptoms not settling in 48 h or concerns
